candidates.title: Exploiting the Flexibility of LLM Inference for Frequency Regulation Service
candidates.abstract: While the widespread deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) has significantly driven up power demands in computing clusters, the unique execution characteristics of LLM inference offer a novel opportunity to utilize these clusters as controllable loads. In this paper, we investigate the potential of LLM inference cluster to provide frequency regulation services through inference request scheduling. First, we model the problem as a hierarchical Markov decision process that includes request-to-replica dispatching and token-level resource allocation. Then, we introduce a reward redistribution network to address the temporal asynchrony between millisecond-level scheduling decisions and second-level frequency regulation signals. Furthermore, we develop an optimization framework based on a mean-field approximation to enable coordination among a large number of replicas under high request concurrency. Simulations using real-world data demonstrate that the proposed approach accurately tracks frequency regulation signals without compromising service-level objectives.
candidates.reason: LLM推論クラスタを電力系統の周波数調整可能な負荷として扱い、要求のreplica配置とtoken単位資源配分を階層MDPで制御する。ミリ秒の推論制御と秒単位の周波数信号をreward redistribution networkで接続し、mean-field近似で多数replicaへ拡張する。著者要旨は実データに基づくシミュレーションでSLOを損なわず周波数調整信号を追従したと報告。推論サービングの電力制御・token schedulingの直接的方式としてaccept。ただし性能値はシミュレーション。

candidates.title: From Overloaded to Guaranteed: High-Throughput Multi-SLO Enforcement for LoRA-Assisted On-Premise LLM Deployment
candidates.abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) become essential in privacy-sensitive sectors like hospitals and government agencies, the on-premise LLM servers offer a cost-effective and secure alternative to public cloud services. However, these resource-constrained servers struggle to guarantee heterogeneous Service Level Objectives (SLOs) when serving multiple LoRA-adapted services simultaneously. Existing serving frameworks suffer from severe SLO violations due to the computational overhead of LoRA layers and the rigid nature of batch scheduling. To address this, we propose HALO, a scheduling method tailored for LoRA-assisted on-premise LLM deployment. HALO introduces two key innovations: a spatial multiplexing strategy that overlaps Base and LoRA computations by partitioning GPU Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs), and an SLO-aware scheduler that decouples request execution based on"request-level slack."By prioritizing urgent tasks and utilizing idle budget for traffic shaping, HALO significantly mitigates resource contention. Our evaluation demonstrates that HALO minimizes SLO violations while improving throughput compared to state-of-the-art baselines.
candidates.reason: 限られたGPU上で複数LoRAサービスを動かすとLoRA演算の競合とbatch schedulerの硬直性がSLO違反を生む。HALOはGPU SMを分割してbaseとLoRA計算を重ね、要求ごとの残りslackに応じて緊急要求を優先し余剰予算でtraffic shapingする。著者要旨は既存方式よりthroughputを上げSLO違反を抑えると報告するが具体的改善率は未記載。複数LoRAのオンプレサービング方式としてaccept。

candidates.title: DySCo: Dynamic Sharding for Collaborative Edge-Cloud LLM Inference with Depth-Synchronized Batching
candidates.abstract: Pervasive intelligent applications are increasingly deployed on mobile and Internet of Things (IoT) edge devices. Consequently, Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support these applications. Yet, due to their high resource demands, LLMs are mostly deployed in the cloud. Layer-wise edge-cloud inference lets resource-constrained edge devices contribute computation to LLMs they cannot host in full. However, heterogeneous split points introduce two coupled inefficiencies. First, edge execution and communication create idle gaps between cloud invocations. Second, requests arriving at different model depths cannot be conventionally batched. We present DySCo, a collaborative runtime that keeps KV caches local and introduces dyForward, a model-aware layer-range executor that runs configurable contiguous layer ranges from resident model shards without reloading weights. For multi-edge serving settings, we introduce depth-synchronized batching (DSB), which advances heterogeneous requests to the deepest cut and batches their common suffix. Experiments across heterogeneous devices, two model families, and local and wide-area links show that idle gaps increase the latency of subsequent GPU forward calls even when waiting time is excluded, adding up to 25 ms of additional cloud-side suffix latency per decoding step in our measurements. At an average concurrency of eight, DSB improves throughput by 275% over FIFO, 48% over exact-match batching, and 79% over round-robin interleaving while reducing mean per-session latency. Together, these results show that requests with different edge-cloud splits can reuse resident cloud weights and share batched suffix computation. The artifact repository for this work is publicly available at: https://github.com/Large-scale-Sustainable-Computing-LSC/dysco-artifact
candidates.reason: 端末ごとにLLMのedge/cloud分割位置が異なると、cloud側のmodel層深度が一致せずbatch化できない問題に対し、resident shardの範囲実行と、異なる要求を最深の共通suffixへ進めてbatch化するdepth-synchronized batchingを提案する。KVは各実行側に保持する。著者要旨は平均8同時要求でFIFO比throughput275%、同一splitだけのbatch比48%改善を報告。edge/cloud協調推論runtimeとしてaccept。

candidates.title: TokenRouter: Efficient Serving System for Token-Level LLM Routing
candidates.abstract: Large language model (LLM) routing distributes inference work across different models, advancing the cost-quality Pareto frontier of LLM serving. While coarse-grained routing at the session or query level has been widely adopted in production systems, recent algorithmic work shows that fine-grained token-level routing can yield substantial efficiency and quality gains. However, efficiently serving token-level routed inference poses significant challenges to existing systems. Built on single-LLM assumptions, current systems suffer from severe step desynchronization and frequent batch admission delays under token-level routing, and they also impose high implementation complexity on developers. To address these challenges, we design TokenRouter, an efficient and developer-friendly serving system for token-level routed LLM inference. TokenRouter follows the principle of request-centric programming, model-centric execution: developers describe routing logic from the perspective of a single request, while the runtime launches a subserver for each LLM and dispatches requests asynchronously. Each subserver employs a delayed-batching scheduler, whose optimal hyperparameters are derived from a mathematical throughput model of the system. Across diverse routing algorithms, workloads, and model pairs, TokenRouter achieves 2.01-64.15x higher decoding throughput than existing systems, substantially advancing the serving efficiency of token-level LLM routing. Our code is available at https://github.com/thu-nics/TokenRouter.
candidates.reason: 生成tokenごとに異なるLLMへ処理を振り分ける際、既存の単一LLM前提runtimeでstep同期とbatch admissionが遅れる問題に対し、request-centricなAPIとモデルごとの非同期subserverを分離する。subserverのdelayed batchingパラメータはthroughputモデルから決める。著者要旨は複数routing方式とモデル組合せで既存方式比decode throughput2.01～64.15倍と報告。複数LLMの細粒度routing実装としてaccept。

candidates.title: Simulate Before You Scale: High-Fidelity LLM Inference Planning Without GPUs
candidates.abstract: Deploying large language model (LLM) inference at scale requires jointly selecting hardware layout, parallelism strategy, scheduling policy, admission control, and request routing to meet latency and throughput targets. These choices interact: a routing decision that improves cache locality can concentrate load, and an admission threshold that triggers only at saturation allows queues to grow deep enough to degrade critical-tier traffic. Evaluating candidates on GPU clusters is too expensive for iterative exploration, yet existing predictive tools either ignore batching and queueing dynamics or model only fragments of the pipeline. In this paper, we present BLIS, a deterministic, CPU-only discrete-event simulator that models the full inference serving pipeline (admission, routing, scheduling, prefill/decode execution, KV-cache management, and preemption). BLIS pairs analytical basis functions with learned scaling coefficients and overhead terms, fit once globally, to predict step latency without per-model or per-GPU profiling. Across 36 experiments spanning six models and three GPU types, BLIS achieves 6.7% median end-to-end error while running around 200 times faster than real execution. In a configuration search over 420 serving configurations for Llama-2-70B, BLIS identifies a 4-GPU deployment that meets a 300ms mean TTFT service-level objective (SLO), whereas competing tools either require double the GPUs or recommend configurations that fail under load. Two policies evolved entirely in simulation were validated on real hardware and merged into llm-d, a widely adopted open-source platform for distributed LLM serving: an admission policy that reduces critical-tier TTFT P90 by up to 82%, and a flow-control policy that reduces E2E P50 latency by 32-48% on overloaded workloads.
candidates.reason: admission・routing・batching・prefill/decode・KV管理・preemptionをCPU-only離散イベントシミュレータBLISへ統合し、モデル/GPUごとの個別profileなしでphase別遅延曲面を予測する。著者要旨は6モデル・3GPUの36実験でend-to-end誤差中央値6.7%、実実行比約200倍のシミュレーション速度と報告。llm-dへ反映された2政策の実機検証も主張する。LLMサービング容量計画・スケジューラ設計の直接的手法としてaccept。
